title: Grateful Dead Live at Pauley Pavilion, UCLA on 1973-11-17
lineage: SBD> MR> C> DAT> CDR> EAC> SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a high‑energy 11/17/73 show highlighted by the legendary Playin’ > Uncle John’s > Morning Dew sandwich and scorching Here Comes Sunshine.
ai_review.review: The recording is a pristine SBD source with crisp, clean mix (only minor hiss or occasional splice), making every nuance of the band audible. Musically the concert is a peak‑era performance – tight first‑set grooves give way to an unstoppable second set featuring the famed Playin’/Uncle John’s/Morning Dew sandwich, soaring Eyes of the World and a blazing Here Comes Sunshine. Energy stays high from start to finish, and the seamless transitions keep the momentum rolling.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 80 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 5 stars, with only a few 4‑star or minor complaints about hiss/splices; both musical performance and recording quality are praised as exceptional.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean mix with excellent instrument separation; occasional slight hiss noted and a brief splice/blank‑space in the UJB segment but these do not detract from overall listenability.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
Playin' in the Band > Uncle John's Band > Morning Dew > Uncle John's Band > Playin'
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds smoothly with strong openers; second set delivers fluid, seamless segues—especially the iconic Playin' sandwich—and maintains a relentless groove throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for leading the improvisational jams, meandering purposefully into the Playin' sandwich and delivering a searing solo on Uncle John's Band.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for “bombs” on Morning Dew and for tightly following/leading Jerry, adding aggressive spice under the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned slashing rhythmically in the background during the jams and delivering soulful vocals on Looks Like Rain and Brown Eyed Women.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboards are generally praised (especially on China Cat > Rider), though a few reviewers note his mix being lower than ideal on this recording.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s hi‑hat work is highlighted as locking in perfectly with Jerry’s intensity, providing a tight rhythmic foundation throughout.
